title: SharePoint forms: Power Automate trigger "When a form is submitted" and action "Get form metadata"
summary: Hold: the claim that whoever holds a document generation form link can submit omits Microsoft's qualification that the sharing experience is for users in the organization. The roadmap facts and both data policy control surfaces are supported, but the specific document-name and location fields attributed to the submission trigger are not documented in the sources checked.

claims.claim: The roadmap introduces the SharePoint operations When a form is submitted and Get form metadata in Power Automate.
claims.quote:
With this update, a new trigger and action are now available in Power Automate:
Trigger: When a form is submitted

claims.quote: This operation triggers a flow when a list form, document generation form, or file upload form is submitted.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the arrival default or whether these operations appear for all makers at once.

claims.claim: The roadmap and Learn sources do not describe a change to existing forms, flows or non-flow-building users.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint forms Power Automate rollout; SharePoint forms Power Automate default available. Read roadmap, SharePoint connector article/reference and document generation page; no existing-form or existing-flow migration/change described.

claims.claim: No admin action or dedicated admin switch for these two new operations is documented in the sources checked.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint forms Power Automate GetTableForm GetOnNewItemsFromForm Set-SPOTenant admin control enable disable. Read connector article/reference, data policy/action-control pages and returned Set-SPOTenant excerpts; no dedicated operation switch found.

claims.claim: Whoever holds a document generation form link can submit.
claims.quote: After you publish the form, share the form link so users in your organization can submit forms and generate documents.
claims.fix: Replace 'so whoever holds the link can submit' with 'and describes sharing the form link with users in your organization'. The source does not establish unrestricted submission by anyone holding a link.

claims.claim: Power Automate does not apply a form's conditional field visibility when generating documents through a flow.
claims.quote: Power Automate doesn't apply conditional visibility: if you generate documents through a Power Automate flow, the flow doesn't hide or show fields the way the form does

claims.claim: A required field hidden by the form remains visible in a document generated through a flow.
claims.quote: so a required field that your form hides will still be visible in the document.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends making normally hidden fields optional when using a form with Power Automate.
claims.quote: When you use a form with Power Automate, make any field you'd normally hide an optional field so it doesn't block the intended flow.
